newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
250,000 STG SCANDAL OF AIDS MAN BRITAIN CAN'T EXPEL

Despite being officially classed as an illegal immigrant, Jose Tadeo dos Santos, 36 who is illiterate, has Aids and suffers from secondary syphilis and highly contagious tuberculosis, is being supported by the state and cannot be deported. The Brazilian arrived in London six years ago.
REBUFF FROM CWS AFTER PROFITS SLUMP

The Co-operative Wholesale Society, Britain's largest Co-op today revealed that its profits have almost halved in a year whilst it has suffered poor sales at its core food stores. Chief Executive of the group Graham Melmoth rebuffed Lanica Trust, who are showing interest in CWS with a view to setting up a hostile bid for non-food businesses.

US RATE-RISE TALK SPURS YEN PROP PROSPECT On expectations that US interest rates will increase, intervention by the Bank of Japan was growing today after the already strong dollar continued to rise against the yen.
PROPERTY SHAKES PUT HK ON SHARES ALERT

Following the first signs that recent real estate fever in Hong Kong is dying down, investors in Hong Kong stocks will be keeping a close watch on the property market this week. The latest data from the States will be examined first for signs of interest rate movements.
